''Ulva plumosa'' (Hudson, 1778) }} '''''Bryopsis plumosa''''', sometimes known by the common names '''green algae''' or '''hen pen''', is a type of green seaweed. == Taxonomy == This species was originally described by [[William Hudson (botanist)|William Hudson]] under the name ''Ulva plumosa''.{{Cite book|url=https://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/52507981|title=Gulielmi Hudsoni, Regiae Societatis Socii et Pharmacopaei Londinensis, Flora anglica : exhibens plantas per regnum Britanniæ sponte crescentes, distributas secundum systema sexuale : cum differentiis specierum, synonymis auctorum, nominibus incolarum, solo locorum, tempore florendi, officinalibus pharmacopæorum.|last=Hudson|first=William|year=1798|location=London|pages=571|doi=10.5962/bhl.title.124875|author-link=William Hudson (botanist)}} ==Distribution== ''Bryopsis plumosa'' is found in the [[British Isles]], Europe, the [[Mediterranean Sea]] and the [[Black Sea]], [[Azores]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], [[France]], [[Norway]], [[Faroes]] and [[Iceland]], on the Atlantic coast of [[North America]], west coast of [[Greenland]], [[Jamaica]], [[Canary Islands]], [[Senegal]], [[Ghana]], [[Mauritania]], [[South Africa]], [[British Columbia]] to [[California]], [[Australia]], [[Japan]] and [[New Zealand]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.habitas.org.uk/marinelife/species.asp?item=ZS3920|title=Bryopsis plumosa - Marine Life Encyclopedia|website=www.habitas.org.uk|access-date=2019-01-24}}{{Cite book|title=New Zealand seaweeds : an illustrated guide|last=W. A.|first=Nelson|publisher=Te Papa Press|year=2013|isbn=9780987668813|location=Wellington, New Zealand|pages=20|oclc=841897290|author-link=Wendy Nelson (marine scientist)}} ==Description== ''Bryopsis plumosa'' has distichous branches with a [[thallus]] that is small and erect, growing up to 10 cm long. It is coloured bright green and has a soft, silky texture. The branches arranged in two opposite rows.Burrows, E.M. 1991. ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 2 Chlorophyta''.{{ISBN|0-565-00981-8}} ==Reproduction== The species is [[dioecious]]; when fertile the male plants turn yellowish-green and the female plants are dark green.Dickinson, C.I. 1963 ''British Seaweeds.'' The Kew Series ==Ecology== It can be found in [[intertidal zone|intertidal pools]]. ==Similar species== ''Bryopsis hypnoides'' can be difficult to distinguish, the branches of ''B. hypnoides'' are arranged spirally or irregularly.Bunker, F.StP, Brodie, J.A., Maggs, C.A. and Bunker, A.R. 2017 ''Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland Second edition''.
